B Avdulla (HAPPY BOYS) pleaded guilty to a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that leaving the 900 Metres he allowed his mount to shift in when not clear of CALL TO COMMAND, resulting in CALL TO COMMAND having to be checked when crowded and also when shifting out blundered when it struck the heels of HAPPY BOYS and further resulting in BASIC INSTINCT having to be checked when crowded between CALL TO COMMAND and SMART TRIO.  Having regard to Jockey Avdulla holding confirmed riding engagements for the remainder of the season and in accordance with previous practices, he was fined the sum of $35,000 in lieu of a one-day suspension.  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his very good race riding record. When questioned regarding his riding in the Home Straight and the reason he elected to shift to the outside of MASTER LUCKY near the 250 Metres, J Orman stated that his instructions were to hold a midfield position but he was issued with no specific instructions as to where to position the horse in the Home Straight.  He said after following HAROLD WIN into the race he observed a run become available between HAROLD WIN and MASTER LUCKY at which point he then started to ride his mount along to improve.  He said under its top weight of 135 lbs JOYFUL JOY did not respond strongly to his efforts and as he was concerned that the run between MASTER LUCKY and HAROLD WIN might close, he elected to shift JOYFUL JOY to the outside of MASTER LUCKY near the 250 Metres to secure clear running.  He added that after making contact with SOLID CAR, his mount became unbalanced before continuing to respond to his riding but did not make any appreciable ground on the first or second placegetters.  Trainer M Newnham confirmed the instructions and stated that, in his opinion, Jockey Orman would have been better suited by persevering for the run between HAROLD WIN and MASTER LUCKY.  After considering his explanations and the manner in which JOYFUL JOY finished the race off, the Stewards advised Jockey Orman that, in their opinion, he had made an error of judgement by shifting to the outside of MASTER LUCKY when the run remained available between MASTER LUCKY and HAROLD WIN.
